title: Operator approval did not apply a finance transaction
original_report: The user wants DeepSeek-driven Operator actions to be executed inside allowed LocalOS boundaries after explicit confirmation. Finance confirmation previously produced a request-only result and did not write the approved transaction.
discovery_scope: Operator tool registry and confirmation flow
ActionOrchestrator capability registry and finance handlers
expected: No finance row exists before confirmation; the approved ActionOrchestrator action creates exactly one transaction in the selected tenant; retry is idempotent.
actual: The Operator routed finance approval to finance.transaction.create, whose documented behavior is request-only and localos_write_performed=false.
environment: Python virtualenv on macOS; production Docker/PostgreSQL smoke on /opt/seo-app
reproduction: A focused handler test requests the dedicated approved finance capability twice, includes a forged payload business_id, and asserts one stored row scoped to the envelope tenant.
failure_signal: Before the fix the capability lookup raised KeyError because no approved apply handler existed.
root_cause: Operator finance.prepare_transaction reused the generic finance.transaction.create proposal capability. That capability deliberately stops at a pending request and therefore cannot apply the confirmed transaction.
fix_summary: Added finance.transaction.apply_operator as a dedicated approval-required ActionOrchestrator capability, validated exactly one finance row, derived business scope only from the envelope tenant, used a stable action-based transaction ID, and routed Operator finance approvals to it.
why_causal: The new handler is the execution target resumed by the same human-approved ActionOrchestrator action; its stable ID and tenant-scoped readback enforce one approved LocalOS write without granting DeepSeek database access.

reproduction_files.summary: Tenant, idempotency, and approved-write regression test.

fix_files.summary: Dedicated approval-required finance apply capability and handler.
Operator finance route now targets the approved apply capability.

checks.name: Focused regression
checks.detail: Same command changed from KeyError to 1 passed.

checks.name: Production runtime
checks.detail: App and worker healthy, HTTP 200, exact file hashes match.

checks.name: Production capability smoke
checks.detail: Handler registered as production_internal_write and Operator route targets it.

limitations: Production smoke did not create a real finance row because that would mutate a business ledger.
The handler applies one transaction per approval; bulk finance import remains a separate governed workflow.
residual_risks: External publication and provider dispatch remain unavailable until dedicated provider-write adapters and approvals exist.
Appointments create_request remains request-only rather than a direct booking write.
notes: DeepSeek receives tool schemas and observations only; it never receives database credentials or unrestricted API access.
The user explicitly approved testing and the production fix in this task.
